pharm: Long-acting depot penicillin G salt; slow IM release gives low but very prolonged serum levels for sustained activity against penicillin-G-sensitive organisms.
quick: Syphilis (early): 2.4 million units IM single dose; strep pharyngitis: 1.2 million units IM once
Used when clearly needed; drug of choice for syphilis in pregnancy
Excretion delayed in impairment; prolonged levels - use caution
Penicillin allergy history; observe for anaphylaxis; serologic response in syphilis
summary: Benzathine penicillin G (Bicillin L-A) is a slowly absorbed depot formulation for DEEP INTRAMUSCULAR injection only, producing low but prolonged serum penicillin levels. It is a first-line agent for syphilis, streptococcal pharyngitis, and rheumatic fever prophylaxis. It carries a boxed warning: it must NEVER be given intravenously or admixed with IV solutions - inadvertent IV administration has caused cardiorespiratory arrest and death. Serious and occasionally fatal anaphylactic reactions can occur, especially in penicillin-allergic patients.
indications: Syphilis, yaws, bejel, and pinta (venereal/treponemal infections)
Mild-to-moderate upper respiratory tract infections due to susceptible group A streptococci (e.g., pharyngitis)
Prophylaxis of rheumatic fever and/or chorea (prevention of recurrence)
Follow-up prophylactic therapy for rheumatic heart disease and acute glomerulonephritis

dosage.c: Syphilis - primary, secondary, or early latent

dosage.n: Total 7.2 million units; benzathine penicillin does not adequately treat neurosyphilis
Ages 2-12: adjust based on adult schedule

dosage.c: Streptococcal (group A) upper respiratory infection - adults

dosage.d: 1,200,000 units monthly OR 600,000 units every 2 weeks

admin: INTRAMUSCULAR INJECTION ONLY - NEVER inject intravenously or admix with IV solutions (risk of cardiorespiratory arrest and death)
Do not inject into or near an artery or nerve
Give by deep IM injection in the upper outer quadrant of the buttock (dorsogluteal) or ventrogluteal site
In neonates, infants, and small children the midlateral thigh may be preferable; anterolateral thigh is not recommended
Inject at a slow, steady rate to avoid needle blockage from the high concentration of suspended material
Vary the injection site when doses are repeated; inspect for particulate matter and discoloration before use
moa: Penicillin G is bactericidal against susceptible organisms during active multiplication by inhibiting biosynthesis of cell-wall peptidoglycan, rendering the cell wall osmotically unstable. The benzathine salt is poorly soluble and hydrolyzed slowly to penicillin G, giving prolonged low serum levels.

absolute: History of a previous hypersensitivity (allergic) reaction to any penicillin
NEVER administer intravenously or admix with IV solutions
relative: History of cephalosporin hypersensitivity or sensitivity to multiple allergens
History of allergy, asthma, hay fever, or urticaria

preg: Reproduction studies in mice, rats, and rabbits showed no evidence of fetal harm; human experience has not shown positive evidence of adverse fetal effects. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed - penicillin remains the treatment of choice for syphilis in pregnancy.
lact: Penicillins are generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; monitor the infant for sensitization, diarrhea, or candidiasis.
renal: With normal renal function the drug is excreted rapidly by tubular excretion. In neonates, young infants, and impaired renal function, excretion is considerably delayed - use with caution as levels are prolonged.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment described in labeling.

major: Tetracyclines (bacteriostatic) may antagonize the bactericidal effect of penicillin - avoid concurrent use
moderate: Probenecid increases and prolongs serum penicillin levels by inhibiting renal tubular secretion and reducing volume of distribution
interactions.diagnostics: May affect serologic monitoring interpretation; follow syphilis titers per guidelines

serious: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SJS, TEN, DRESS, AGEP)
Kounis syndrome (acute myocardial ischemia as part of allergic reaction)
rare: Serum sickness-like reactions (chills, fever, edema, arthralgia, prostration)
emergency: Anaphylaxis (including shock and death) requiring immediate epinephrine
Cardiorespiratory arrest and death from inadvertent IV administration
Penicillin overdose: neuromuscular hyperirritability or convulsive seizures

monitoring: Careful inquiry about prior penicillin, cephalosporin, or other allergen hypersensitivity before each dose
Observation for immediate hypersensitivity / anaphylaxis after injection
Confirm IM (not intravascular) placement before injecting
Serologic (nontreponemal titer) follow-up in syphilis to confirm response
Watch for persistent or severe diarrhea (possible CDAD)
counsel: This medicine is given as a deep injection into muscle - it is never given into a vein
Tell your clinician about any allergy to penicillin or cephalosporin antibiotics
Seek emergency care for difficulty breathing, swelling, rash, or fainting after the injection
When treated for syphilis you may get fever, chills, and headache within hours (Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction) - this usually settles
Keep all follow-up and repeat-dose appointments and complete any required blood-test follow-up
pk: Slow; depot release from IM site
Low serum levels reached over hours; very prolonged plateau
Effectively prolonged by slow absorption (hydrolysis-limited release)
300,000 units: levels 4-5 days; 600,000 units: ~10 days; 1,200,000 units: ~14 days (detectable up to 4 weeks)
Refrigerate; do not freeze; inspect before use
pearls: BOXED WARNING: never give IV or admix with IV solutions - inadvertent IV use has caused cardiorespiratory arrest and death
First-line for syphilis: 2.4 million units IM single dose for primary/secondary/early latent; weekly x3 for late latent
Benzathine penicillin does NOT achieve adequate CNS levels - it is not appropriate for neurosyphilis
Not active against penicillinase-producing organisms or beta-lactam-resistant bacteria
No resistance to penicillin G has been reported in Streptococcus pyogenes
Approximately 0.11 mEq sodium per 600,000 units; about 60% protein-bound
missed: For rheumatic fever / recurrent infection prophylaxis, give the missed injection as soon as possible and resume the regular schedule. Do not give extra doses to make up. Therapeutic (single-dose) syphilis and strep regimens are completed by appointment.
overdose: Penicillin in overdose may cause neuromuscular hyperirritability or convulsive seizures. Discontinue and provide supportive care; manage seizures with anticonvulsants. Penicillin G is dialyzable.
